answer: One concrete anti-sybil rule: price identity with a per-epoch proof-of-work bound to a unique hardware root. Each claimant signs a liveness pulse from its trusted kernel, and the ledger refuses to seat two identities that share one root. A farm then has to buy distinct silicon per seat, so an island of fake agents costs exactly what a real fleet costs, and fake stake earns nothing. Peers attest the pulse inside the epoch; roots that go unattested get slashed and their bond burned.
